positions.claim: The bottleneck on AI's impact is diffusing existing capability through the world, not further model progress.
If models never improved beyond today, there would still be decades of upheaval in the economy and how the world operates.
Startups that properly embrace agents can easily outcompete incumbents; the dynamic is now Goliath-versus-Goliath rather than David-versus-Goliath.
Successful companies are started long before their core idea is consensus, and founders must toil in obscurity for years.
Scale's early idea (an AI agent for getting medical care) was right but mistimed, and is only viable now.
Talent density was the core thing to bet on in rebuilding Meta's lab, and it compounds because talented people attract more talented people.
Frontier AI work is scientific research and requires a different mindset and operating model than internet product companies.
Each AI wave has been roughly 10x bigger than the last: self-driving, then chatbots, then coding agents.
The best AI products have not been developed yet.
Models should not be priced so high that they are rationed to only the wealthiest developers and companies.
Meta will ship larger models competitive with the best available, open-source models, and its own agent harness focused on speed, reliability, and extensibility.
Debating exactly when superintelligence arrives, or whether progress hits a wall, is largely a waste of time because powerful models are inevitable.
Intelligence and agency will become abundant, making vision and ambition the scarce resources.
Going all in on verbal skills at the expense of quantitative and systems thinking is a mistake, because systems thinking survives every shift in abstraction layer.
Humanity will probably change more in the next decade than it has in the past 100 years.
A correctly designed agentic loop with the right eval or metric can accomplish more than a team of 100 engineers.
Building high-leverage agent systems is mechanically mundane: pick the metric, then use skills, markdown files, and cron jobs.
Builders have a responsibility to prepare enterprises and governments and to address biosecurity and cybersecurity risks, not just ship capability.
Meta's Spark model is roughly 8x cheaper than Opus.
Working at a company before founding one is valuable because you otherwise have no idea how companies build, iterate, or make decisions.
The right thing to work on is whatever exponential has the steepest curve and the longest runway, even if its starting point looks boring.
